endorsements.quote: Ensure consent processes reflect the full scope of the tool's function, including the generation of observations and diagnostic impressions, not only audio recording for documentation.
Validate each tool as deployed; equivalent benchmark performance does not imply equivalent behaviour in use.10
Review and edit the draft while unvoiced observations and judgments remain retrievable.
Search the draft for what is absent as well as what is wrong; omissions in fluent text may be harder to notice than errors.

unlisted_practices: Provide provenance labels for every field of AI-generated notes, distinguishing transcribed content from inferred content and recording the basis for each inference.
Do not populate by default mental status fields that the available input cannot support; suppress them or flag them for clinician entry.
Allow each AI scribe operation (narrative, observation, assessment and plan) to be enabled, reviewed, and evaluated independently.
Support capture of clinicians' own observations during or soon after the encounter so direct findings enter the note.
Offer configurations that preserve designated note sections, particularly the assessment, as clinician-generated.
Clinicians should record observations the recording cannot contain, ideally before reading the AI draft.
Clinicians should form and note an independent impression before reading the AI-generated assessment.
Clinicians should verbalise the assessment and plan at the close of the encounter so the tool transcribes stated reasoning rather than generating unstated reasoning.
Clinicians should treat AI-generated mental status content as inference until confirmed against direct observation.
Clinicians should review AI-generated history for therapeutic appropriateness, clinical nuance, and legal weight of word choice, not only factual accuracy.
Regulators should consider whether AI-generated diagnostic reasoning in documentation tools warrants classification as a medical device with differentiated regulatory scrutiny.

screen.reason: This is a Personal View / perspective paper discussing the clinical oversight, informed consent, liability, and regulatory implications of ambient AI scribes in psychiatry.
